risks.description: A single relational database is a single-region availability and durability boundary.
risks.mitigation: Use managed storage, backups and replication in production; multi-region active-active is required for a 99.999% target.

risks.description: An in-memory cache is local to one process and can become cold after restart.
risks.mitigation: Use cache-aside semantics and retain the database as the source of truth.

risks.description: The bounded analytics queue can drop click events under sustained overload.
risks.mitigation: Expose dropped-event metrics and move to durable messaging when analytics completeness becomes mandatory.

risks.description: Generated short codes based on sequential IDs are enumerable.
risks.mitigation: Use opaque random identifiers or an encoding strategy that does not expose database sequencing in production.

risks.description: Unauthenticated link creation can enable spam and abuse.
risks.mitigation: Add authentication, API keys, rate limiting and abuse controls before internet-scale deployment.

failureScenarios.detection: Database connection errors and failed health checks
failureScenarios.mitigation: Fail creation explicitly, preserve redirect cache hits where possible, and restore database availability.
Drop analytics events without failing redirects and scale or replace the queue when required.

failureScenarios.detection: URL validation failure during link creation
failureScenarios.mitigation: Accept only URLs with http or https schemes and a valid host.

failureScenarios.detection: Increased database lookup rate and redirect latency
failureScenarios.mitigation: Use cache-aside loading from the durable store.

validationStrategy: Unit tests cover Base62 encoding, URL validation, alias validation, duplicate aliases and click recording.
Integration tests cover H2 persistence, analytics aggregation and HTTP redirect behavior.
Run the complete Maven build and test suite through the controlled validation runner.
Perform a load or failure-injection check against the redirect and analytics paths before production deployment.
tradeoffs: H2 and JDBC keep the reference implementation dependency-light but are not a production HA database deployment.
Best-effort asynchronous analytics protects redirect latency at the cost of possible event loss.
A local cache improves hot-read latency but does not provide distributed cache consistency.
